result.stdout:
Usage: rony run <config.json> [options]

Starts the mock server described by the file (see the Configuration Files wiki page), prints where it listens
and logs every connection and request, until Ctrl+C or SIGTERM.
  --port <N>       Port (default: from the file; 0 is a free port)
  --address <ip>   Address (default: from the file)
  --journal <file> Append every received request to the file, one JSON object per line
  --keep <N>       Requests and connection records kept in memory (default 10000; 0 is unlimited)
  --control <N>    Control endpoint on 127.0.0.1:<N> (0 is a free port): read the received requests and the state
  --control-address <ip>  Address of the control endpoint (default 127.0.0.1; it has no authentication)
  --watch          Reload the rules when the file changes
  --quiet          Do not print the log lines

result.stdout:
Usage: rony replay <recording.json> [options]

Serves a recording as a mock server, until Ctrl+C or SIGTERM.
  --port <N>             Port (default 0: a free port)
  --address <ip>         Address (default 127.0.0.1)
  --tls                  Serve TLS with a generated self-signed certificate
  --journal <file>       Append every received request to the file, one JSON object per line
  --keep <N>             Requests and connection records kept in memory (default 10000; 0 is unlimited)
  --control <N>          Control endpoint on 127.0.0.1:<N> (0 is a free port): read the received requests and the state
  --control-address <ip> Address of the control endpoint (default 127.0.0.1; it has no authentication)
  --quiet                Do not print the log lines
Framing (at most one; default: none):
  --delimiter <text>      Messages end with this text; \n \r \t \\ \0 and \xNN are interpreted
  --length-prefix <1|2|4> Messages start with a big-endian length of 1, 2 or 4 bytes
  --stx-etx               Messages are wrapped in STX (0x02) and ETX (0x03)
